# fluid error codes

Every failure prints a stable `ERR_<EVENT>` code next to its message. Find the
code here and do what the first suggestion says, then re-run the command. A code
missing from this table has no curated advice: read the message it printed.
`fluid validate --format json` gives every finding in a contract as an entry of
`issues`, with its code, a JSON `pointer` to the place, a `fix` and an `example`:
the `ERR_CONTRACT_*` codes below.
Docs pages are relative to https://agenticstiger.github.io/forge_docs/

| Code | What to do | Docs page |
|---|---|---|
| `ERR_ODCS_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` | Pass one of the versions the message lists: --odcs-version 3.1.0 (the default) or 3.2.0. 3.2.0 adds the Iceberg server type; a catalog that validates v3.1.0 only needs the default. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DOCTOR_PREFLIGHT_FAILED` | Run 'fluid doctor --contract contract.fluid.yaml --operation plan'. Compare two saved reports with 'fluid doctor --compare left.json right.json'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_NOT_SPECIFIED` | Pass a provider: --provider aws\|databricks\|gcp\|local\|snowflake. Or set the FLUID_PROVIDER environment variable. Run 'fluid providers' to list the available providers. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND` | Run 'fluid providers' to see the available providers. Check the provider name spelling. Install the provider extra, e.g. pip install 'data-product-forge[gcp]'. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN` | Run 'fluid providers' to see the available providers. Valid built-ins: aws, databricks, gcp, local, snowflake. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_LOAD_FAILED` | The provider is declared but importing it failed (see the WARNING above). Reinstall the distribution named in the error, or its extra. Run 'fluid providers --debug' for the discovery errors. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_RETIRED` | Run 'fluid providers' to see the available providers. CHANGELOG.md lists it under Removed, with its replacement. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | If a job outside forge-cli (a Flink job, say) writes that expose or is that build, declare the build with engine: flink (or properties.language: flink_sql) and outputs naming what it writes: forge-cli then leaves both to the job. --provider <name> (or FLUID_PROVIDER) applies the whole contract with the provider you name; the local provider writes a binding it does not serve as a placeholder file. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_PLAN_DIGEST_MAINTENANCE_ACTIONS_CHANGED` | A maintenance action's statements are not the ones the plan bound: the plugin that renders them changed since fluid plan. Run fluid plan again with the packages apply runs with, then apply that plan. To see what the action runs now, run fluid apply --mode maintain --expose-id <expose> --dry-run on the contract. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_PLAN_RUNS_OUTSIDE_FORGE` | In the default mode, apply the contract file instead (fluid apply contract.fluid.yaml): the local planner plans it, and leaves what a job outside forge-cli writes to that job. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_BLOCKED_BY_POLICY` | This provider is named in FLUID_PLUGINS_BLOCKLIST, or an FLUID_PLUGINS_ALLOWLIST is set and does not name it. Run 'fluid plugins --role provider' to see the effective policy. Unset or amend the env var to re-enable it. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_RESERVED_PROVIDER_NAME` | Choose a provider name that is not a reserved built-in. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_REQUIRED` | Pass the contract path: fluid <command> path/to/contract.fluid.yaml. Or run from a directory that contains a single contract.fluid.yaml. Scaffold one with 'fluid init' or 'fluid forge'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND` | Check that the contract file path is correct. Ensure the file has a .yaml, .yml, or .json extension. Scaffold one with 'fluid init' or 'fluid forge'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_FILE_NOT_FOUND` | Check that the contract file path is correct. Run 'ls *.fluid.yaml' to see contracts in the current directory. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_LOAD_FAILED` | Verify the YAML/JSON syntax is valid. Check file permissions and that the encoding is UTF-8. Run 'fluid validate <contract>' for a detailed report. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DMM_BATCH_NO_CONTRACTS` | A folder is searched for files named *.fluid.yaml, *.fluid.yml or *.fluid.json at any depth. Check the folder path, or name the contract files or a glob pattern instead. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DMM_BATCH_DUPLICATE_PRODUCT` | Give each contract its own product id, or leave the extra copy out of the run. Run 'fluid validate <contract>' on each file named above. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DMM_BATCH_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE` | Remove one consumes[] entry from the loop: a product cannot consume a product that consumes it. Run 'fluid dmm publish <folder> --dry-run' again to check the order. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DMM_VERIFY_REPORT_UNREADABLE` | Pass a report written by 'fluid verify <contract> --out report.json'. Or pass the folder that holds the reports: files in it that are not verify reports are skipped. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DMM_PROMOTE_NOTHING_NAMED` | Name the products to promote: 'fluid dmm promote products/' or 'fluid dmm promote --id <product-id>'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DMM_PROMOTE_CONTRACT_WITHOUT_ID` | A contract needs a top-level id to name its product; run 'fluid validate <contract>'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION` | Use a supported version (current line: 0.7.x) in fluidVersion or --schema-version. Run 'fluid validate --list-versions' to see the supported versions. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_SCHEMA_VERSION_REQUIRED` | Name the version: fluid validate --fragment KIND <file> --schema-version <version>. Run 'fluid validate --list-versions' to see the supported versions. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_FILE_REQUIRED` | Give the kind, then the file: fluid validate --fragment expose <file>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_BUNDLE_UNSUPPORTED` | Validate the bundle without --fragment: fluid validate <bundle>.tgz. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_KIND_UNKNOWN` | Use one of the kinds the error lists, for example: fluid validate --fragment expose <file>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_ENV_UNSUPPORTED` | Validate the whole contract with the overlay: fluid validate contract.fluid.yaml --env <env>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_HAS_POINTERS` | Validate the contract that uses the fragment: fluid validate contract.fluid.yaml. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_DIAGNOSTICS_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED` | Validate one contract at a time: fluid validate <product>/contract.fluid.yaml --format sarif. Or drop --diagnostics / --format sarif to validate the workspace or bundle as a whole. Run --list-versions or --show-schema without --format sarif. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_SCHEMA_NOT_AVAILABLE` | Run 'fluid validate --list-versions' to see the versions this CLI has. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` | Migrate the contract to the current 0.7.x schema. Pre-0.7 contracts (0.4.0 / 0.5.x) are no longer supported. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_INVALID_MIN_VERSION` | Give --min-version a version constraint, for example --min-version '>=0.7.0'. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_INVALID_MAX_VERSION` | Give --max-version a version constraint, for example --max-version '<0.8.0'. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract> --verbose' for the full error list. Check required fields and the schema reference for your fluidVersion. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_VALIDATION_ERROR` | Run 'fluid validate <contract> --verbose' for details. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_NOT_FOUND` | Run 'fluid bundle <contract> --format tgz' to produce a bundle first. Check the bundle path you passed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_MANIFEST_INVALID` | Re-create the bundle with 'fluid bundle' — the manifest is malformed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_MISSING_CONTRACT` | Re-create the bundle with 'fluid bundle' — it has no contract entry. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PRODUCT_ID_CHANGED` | If the id changed by mistake, set it back to the baseline's value: the id is the product's identity, so the contract then stays the same product. A new id is a second product: the old catalog entry stays, apply state and run cursors start over, and a consumes[].productId that names the old id keeps pointing at it. If the rename is intended, run 'fluid diff <contract> --baseline <baseline>' without --fail-on-id-change, then update every consumes[].productId that names the old id and retire the old catalog entry. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PLANNER_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>' first to rule out a contract problem. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_BUILD_IDENTIFIER_INVALID` | Rename the id to fit, for example orders_v1 instead of 1orders, and apply again. A renamed id starts over: its builds get new cursors and watermarks under .fluid/runs/, and a renamed contract.id gets a new OpenTofu workdir under .fluid/iac/<provider>/. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_BUILD_ID_NOT_FOUND` | Pass one of the available build ids as --build-id: ids match exactly, case included. Run 'fluid apply <contract> --mode amend-and-build' without --build-id to run every build. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_SPARK_ROLLBACK_UNSAFE` | The release moved the stream's checkpoint (properties.stream.checkpoint) and the previous config writes the same output, so forge did not start it again: it would resume its old checkpoint from before the offsets the new run reached, and write those records into the output a second time. The failed run is cancelled and the stream is down. To go back on purpose, apply the previous contract again (fluid apply <previous contract>) and expect the records between the two checkpoints twice; to go on, fix the contract and run fluid apply. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_SPARK_NO_KNOWN_GOOD_CONFIG` | The config this release replaced did not end well (its last run failed, was cancelled before the apply, or was lost), so it is no config to go back to, and the stream is down. Fix the contract and run fluid apply. The failed run's outcome names its error; its logs are in the run's runtime. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_SPARK_RELEASE_FAILED_EARLIER` | This config failed its probation on an earlier fluid apply and is not started again as it stands: change the contract to fix it, and run fluid apply. When the cause was the environment, not the config, set FLUID_SPARK_ACCEPT_FAILED_RELEASE=1 for one fluid apply (the operator's environment, not a project .env) to start it again. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_SPARK_ARTIFACT_READ_DENIED` | Grant the identity that runs fluid apply s3:GetObject on the build's prefix (_fluid/spark/<product>/<build>/): forge reads the failed-release marker and the job config there, and refused to start anything it cannot check. Also grant s3:ListBucket, scoped to the release prefix (the build's _fluid/spark/<product>/<build>/ and nothing wider): without it S3 answers a missing object with AccessDenied, and a refused marker cannot be told from a missing one. Only the marker refused while the job config reads: set FLUID_SPARK_ACCEPT_FAILED_RELEASE=1 for one fluid apply (the operator's environment, not a project .env) to start without knowing whether the config failed its probation. That override also skips a real failed-release marker, so never set it permanently, in a keepalive's environment least of all. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OUTPUT_WRITE_FAILED` | Check that the --out path is writable and the parent directory exists. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_ENGINE_INSTALL_FAILED` | Install OpenTofu >= 1.12.0 and ensure 'tofu' is on PATH. See https://opentofu.org/docs/intro/install/. | getting-started/ |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_INIT_FAILED` | Check provider credentials and network access, then retry. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_PLAN_FAILED` | Run 'fluid plan <contract>' and inspect the emitted plan for the failing action. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_APPLY_FAILED` | OpenTofu records state as it goes, so resources created before the failure are normally tracked. Fix the cause named above, then re-run 'fluid apply' to continue. Re-run with --debug to see the raw tofu output. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_ADOPTION_FAILED` | Check the provider credentials and network access, then re-run 'fluid apply'. The apply stopped before planning: it could not tell whether the object exists, and creating over it would replace it. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_TABLE_ADOPTION_REQUIRES_FLAG` | Review the take-over first: 'fluid plan <contract> --tofu --adopt-tables' checks each table against the contract and saves the plan. Then apply that plan with 'fluid apply plan.json', or re-run this apply with --adopt-tables. A table forge made that names no product (from a contract over 50 KB, before forge recorded the id): if it is this product's, add the Glue table parameter fluid_product_id=<the contract's id> once, with the table's writers paused, through 'aws glue update-table' with --version-id from a fresh 'aws glue get-table', so a concurrent commit fails instead of being reverted; or, where the run can pass flags and keeps its state, run once with --adopt-tables. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TABLE_ADOPTION_MISMATCH` | Nothing was imported or applied: the tables are as they were. Align exposes[].contract.schema and binding.location with each table named above, then re-run with --adopt-tables. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TABLE_ADOPTION_UNAVAILABLE` | Set AWS_ACCOUNT_ID to the account that holds the tables, or run with credentials sts:GetCallerIdentity accepts, then re-run with --adopt-tables. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_PLAN_ADOPT_TABLES_NEEDS_TOFU` | Run 'fluid plan <contract> --tofu --adopt-tables'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_ICEBERG_TABLE_UPDATE_IN_PLACE` | Nothing was applied: the tables are as they were. Change the table through its Iceberg catalog (an ALTER TABLE in Spark or Athena): Iceberg's commit updates Glue with the version it read, so a concurrent commit fails instead of being reverted. Or change the contract to describe the table as it is. Or pause the table's writers and re-run with --allow-iceberg-update; for a saved plan, make it again with 'fluid plan <contract> --tofu' (it leaves the table as it is) or add --allow-iceberg-update there. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PLAN_ALLOW_ICEBERG_UPDATE_NEEDS_TOFU` | Run 'fluid plan <contract> --tofu --allow-iceberg-update', or give the flag to the 'fluid apply' that plans again. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_REGION_MOVED` | If the resources should stay where they are, set the binding's location.region to the region the error names. If they should move, empty and remove them there first (tofu destroy in the state directory the error names, with AWS_REGION set to the old region), then apply again. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_MISSING_LLM_API_KEY` | Run 'fluid ai setup' to configure a provider interactively. Or set a provider key: OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY. For local models: --llm-provider ollama (no key required). For keyless authoring: --llm-provider claude-code. | cli/secrets.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_NO_LLM_PROVIDER` | Pass --llm-provider, for example anthropic, openai, gemini or ollama. Or set FLUID_LLM_PROVIDER, or the API key of exactly one provider. Or run 'fluid ai setup' to choose and save a provider. Run 'fluid doctor' to see what forge would select. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_LITELLM_UNAVAILABLE` | Run 'fluid doctor' to see which optional packages are installed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_MCP_SDK_UNAVAILABLE` | Run 'fluid doctor' to see which optional packages are installed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_NOT_VALID_JSON` | Fix the JSON syntax in the named .claude/settings.json (or settings.local.json). Re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target claude-code. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_UNEXPECTED_SHAPE` | The named settings file must be a JSON object; if it has 'hooks', that must be an object, and 'hooks.PostToolUse' a list of objects. Fix the file, then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target claude-code. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_LINKS_OUTSIDE_PROJECT` | The named Claude Code settings file is a symlink to a file outside this project; scaffold-ide would copy that file's content into the project. Replace the link with a regular file or delete it, then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target claude-code. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCAFFOLD_IDE_FILE_NOT_UTF8` | Re-save the named CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md as UTF-8. Then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target <target>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCAFFOLD_IDE_BLOCK_MARKERS_MALFORMED` | The named CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md must hold either no scaffold-ide markers or exactly one '<!-- BEGIN forge-cli scaffold-ide block -->' followed by one matching END marker. Delete the stray or duplicate marker lines (the file was left untouched), then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target <target>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_REFUSING_TO_OVERWRITE_EXISTING_FILE_PASS_FORCE_TO_OVERRIDE` | Re-run with --force to replace the file: fluid scaffold-ide --target <target> --force. --force keeps the text of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md outside the scaffold-ide block. Upgrading? --force also removes the steering files an earlier scaffold-ide wrote. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPTIONAL_DEPENDENCY_MISSING` | Run 'fluid doctor' to see which optional packages are installed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_MISSING_LLM_MODEL` | Set FLUID_LLM_MODEL or pass --llm-model. Run 'fluid ai setup' to pick a default model. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_LLM_MODEL_PREFLIGHT_FAILED` | Check the provider API key and network connectivity. For Ollama, start the local server and pull the requested model. Pass --llm-model with a known-available model. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND` | Run 'fluid ai setup' to pick a model the provider actually serves. List the provider's models, then pass --llm-model <name>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_MISSING_CONTRACT` | Pass the contract path: fluid <command> path/to/contract.fluid.yaml. Or run from a directory that contains a single contract.fluid.yaml. Scaffold one with 'fluid init' or 'fluid forge'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_LOADER_IMPORT_FAILED` | Check that the loader module path is importable (on PYTHONPATH). Verify the module has no syntax/import errors: python -c 'import <module>'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_LOADER_MISSING_FUNCTIONS` | The loader module must define the required entry-point functions — check its API. Define the expected functions (e.g. load/run) — see the custom-loader docs. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_ENGINE_MISSING` | Install the engine: pip install 'data-product-forge[custom-scaffold]'. Or leave custom-scaffold out of --emit to generate the other artifacts. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_CHANGE_REQUEST` | Leave custom-scaffold out of --emit on pull and merge request builds: fluid ship does that by itself. Pass --allow-scaffold-on-change-request only when the build's changes are trusted. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_ENGINE_BROKEN` | The engine is installed but one of its own dependencies is missing or broken: pip install --force-reinstall 'data-product-forge[custom-scaffold]'. Or leave custom-scaffold out of --emit to generate the other artifacts. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_ENGINE_TOO_OLD` | Upgrade the engine: pip install --upgrade 'data-product-forge[custom-scaffold]'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_CONTRACT_INVALID` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>' to list every problem in extensions.customScaffold. Every pattern's use: must name a library the block declares (<library id>:<pattern>). | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_PLUGIN_BLOCKED` | An entrypoint bundle is an installed plugin: the operator allows it in FLUID_PLUGINS_ALLOWLIST and must not list it in FLUID_PLUGINS_BLOCKLIST. Or name the bundle by a path or git source instead. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_BUNDLE_FAILED` | Check the library's source: a relative path: source is read from the contract's directory. A git source with auth needs its host in FLUID_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_AUTH_HOSTS and a secret_ref that starts with FLUID_SCAFFOLD_, both set where the command runs. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_PLAN_FAILED` | A pattern failed to render: check the variables it passes and the contract fields its templates read. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_UNSAFE_PATH` | A template's to: path must stay inside the output: no absolute path, no '..'. The scaffold may write regular files only: no links. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_APPLY_FAILED` | Check that --out is a directory this user can write to. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_OUTPUT_FAILED` | The engine reported files that differ from what it wrote: re-run; if it repeats, the bundle's plugin writes outside its plan. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CUSTOM_SCAFFOLD_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>' first to rule out a contract problem. Re-run with --log-level DEBUG to see the engine's own log. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_PYSPARK_SCHEMA_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>' first to rule out a contract problem. Check that --out is a directory this user can write to. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_PYSPARK_SCHEMA_FOREIGN_FILE` | A file with a module's name is already in --out and this command did not write it, so it is left alone: move it away, or choose another --out. Files this command wrote start with its '# Generated by' line and are replaced when the contract changes. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_PYSPARK_SCHEMA_OTHER_PRODUCT` | A module with this name is already in --out and was generated for another data product, so it is left alone and nothing is written: give each product its own --out, for example runtime/pyspark_schema/<product>. Or delete the file if that product no longer uses this --out: this command never replaces a module another product generated. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_PYSPARK_SCHEMA_DRIFT` | Run 'fluid generate pyspark-schema <contract> --out <dir>' and commit the modules it writes. Delete a module listed as no longer in the contract: the command never deletes. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>' first to rule out a contract problem. Re-run with --provider explicitly set if auto-detect picked the wrong cloud. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` | Drop --provider and let the cloud auto-detect from the contract's binding. Or change the contract's exposes[].binding.platform to the cloud you meant to target — that is how a data product is retargeted, not --provider. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_EMPTY_MODULE` | Check the contract's exposes[].binding carries the location fields the target cloud's emitter needs (bucket/dataset/database). Run 'fluid validate <contract>' — the Iceberg and Confluent binding gates name the specific field a skipped resource was missing. Pass --allow-empty only if a resource-free module is genuinely intended. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_AWS_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` | Set AWS_ACCOUNT_ID to the account the module will be applied in, then re-run 'fluid generate iac' (it never looks the account up in AWS). 'fluid apply' resolves the account itself and needs no AWS_ACCOUNT_ID. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_CI_FAILED` | Check the --system value is a supported CI provider and the contract validates. Run 'fluid validate <contract>', then re-run with a supported --system (github_actions\|gitlab\|jenkins\|azure_devops\|...). | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_NO_BUILDS` | No build runners matched — check the contract's build/transform config. Run 'fluid apply <contract> --mode amend-and-build' only when builds are defined. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_VERIFY_FAILED` | Run 'fluid verify <contract> --verbose' to see which reconciliation check failed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_POLICY_COMPILE_FAILED` | Check the agent-policy block in the contract; run 'fluid policy check <contract>'. | concepts/sovereignty.html |
| `ERR_POLICY_COMPILER_CRASHED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>': policy compile reads accessPolicy and exposes without validating them against the contract schema. If the contract validates, re-run with 'fluid --log-level DEBUG policy compile <contract>' to see the compiler's traceback. | cli/policy-compile.html#errors |
| `ERR_POLICY_APPLY_FAILED` | Run 'fluid policy check <contract>' to surface the offending rule before apply. | concepts/sovereignty.html |
| `ERR_SOVEREIGNTY_VIOLATION` | Move the offending binding into an allowed region, or widen 'sovereignty.allowedRegions' in the contract. Run 'fluid validate <contract>' to see the same findings with full detail. Set 'sovereignty.enforcementMode: advisory' to report a region outside 'allowedRegions' without blocking; a region in 'deniedRegions' blocks in every mode. Pass --no-check-sovereignty to write the plan anyway (logged at WARNING; fluid apply keeps its own checks). | concepts/sovereignty.html |
| `ERR_PRODUCT_NEW_FAILED` | Check the target directory is writable and the productType is valid (SDP/ADP/CDP). Pick an empty/new target dir and pass --data-product-type SDP\|ADP\|CDP explicitly. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PRODUCT_ADD_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate' on the contract first; --type must be source\|exposure\|dq. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PRODUCT_ADD_EXPOSE_NOT_FOUND` | The --expose target does not exist in the contract — list exposes with 'fluid status'. Add the expose first, or target an existing exposeId. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_SOURCE_MISSING` | Re-create the bundle with 'fluid bundle' — a referenced source file is absent. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_LOAD_FAILED` | The bundle is corrupt or truncated — re-create it with 'fluid bundle <contract>'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_MARKET_DISCOVERY_FAILED` | Check network access to the marketplace endpoint (FLUID_MARKET_URL). Bundled blueprints work offline: 'fluid market --blueprints'. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_MISSING_BLUEPRINT_PARAMETER` | The blueprint requires a parameter — pass it with --param key=value. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SIGNING_BUNDLE_MISSING` | Produce the bundle first ('fluid bundle <contract> --format tgz'), then sign it. | cli/verify-signature.html |
| `ERR_SIGNING_BUNDLE_NOT_FILE` | The signing target must be a bundle file, not a directory. Produce one with 'fluid bundle <contract> --format tgz', then sign that .tgz. | cli/verify-signature.html |
| `ERR_SIGNING_KEY_REF_EMPTY` | Provide a signing key reference (e.g. a cosign key or KMS key URI). See the signing setup in the supply-chain docs. | cli/verify-signature.html |
| `ERR_VALIDATE_ARTIFACTS_INPUT_MISSING` | Pass the generated-artifacts path produced by 'fluid generate artifacts'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_DAGS_DIR_MISSING` | Pass --dags-dir pointing at your Airflow DAGs directory. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_DAGS_DIR_NOT_DIRECTORY` | The --dags-dir value must be an existing directory. Create it (mkdir -p) or point --dags-dir at your Airflow dags/ folder. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_UNHANDLED_SCHEME` | Use a supported destination scheme (file / scp / git+ssh) for --to. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_FLAGS` | Add --airflow-url <Airflow API server URL> to run the Airflow check, or drop the --airflow-* / --check-only flags. --airflow-bundle and --airflow-bundle-version need Airflow 3 (DAG bundles). | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEDULER` | Run the Airflow check with --scheduler airflow, astronomer or composer. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_NO_DAG_FILES` | Point --dags-dir at the DAG files fluid generate schedule wrote. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_BAD_URL` | Pass --airflow-url as https://<host>[/<prefix>], with no user name, password, query or fragment. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_INSECURE_URL` | Use an https:// --airflow-url. Or set FLUID_AIRFLOW_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true in the operator environment where plain HTTP is intended. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_CREDENTIALS` | Set FLUID_AIRFLOW_TOKEN_REF (a token) or FLUID_AIRFLOW_CREDENTIAL_REF (user:password) to a secret reference such as env://NAME, not both. Run fluid secrets check to see why a reference does not resolve. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_UNREACHABLE` | Check that the Airflow API server answers at --airflow-url from this machine. A restarting server answers 502/503 for a while: raise --airflow-wait or re-run. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_API_NOT_FOUND` | Pass the root URL of Airflow's API server (Airflow 2: the webserver); include a path prefix it is served under. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_API_MISMATCH` | Leave --airflow-api at auto, or pass v2 for Airflow 3 and v1 for Airflow 2. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` | Check that --airflow-url is an Airflow 2.x or 3.x API server. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_AUTH_FAILED` | Check the secret behind FLUID_AIRFLOW_CREDENTIAL_REF or FLUID_AIRFLOW_TOKEN_REF. Airflow 2 takes a password only with airflow.api.auth.backend.basic_auth in [api] auth_backends; Airflow 3 issues a token from POST /auth/token. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_FORBIDDEN` | Give the Airflow user or token read access to DAGs and import errors (Viewer). | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_REDIRECT` | Pass the URL the redirect points at as --airflow-url; a sign-in page means a proxy sits in front of Airflow. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_BAD_RESPONSE` | Check that --airflow-url points at Airflow's API server, not another service. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_IMPORT_ERRORS` | Fix the import error the report names, then re-run fluid schedule-sync. Parse the DAG locally against the same Airflow major before pushing. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_NOT_PARSED` | Raise --airflow-wait: Airflow lists new files every dag_dir_list_interval (Airflow 2) or refresh_interval (Airflow 3), 300 s by default. On an Airflow 3 Git bundle, check that it tracks the branch the push went to. Where a file waits for Airflow's stored source, check that Airflow parses the folder or bucket the push wrote to. A file forge reads no DAG id from is waited for like a DAG factory when its import makes any call; move a helper module like that out of --dags-dir (plugins/, or a package installed with Airflow). | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_AIRFLOW_UNPROVEN` | Let the Airflow user read DAG code (the 'can read on DAG Code' permission with the FAB auth manager), so the check can compare the source Airflow stores with the pushed file. On Airflow 2, keep [core] store_dag_code on (the default). | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_ROLLBACK_PRODUCT_ID_EMPTY` | Pass the product id to roll back: fluid rollback <product-id>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_TABLE_INVALID` | Name the table as catalog.schema.table, e.g. --results-table ops.dq.fluid_test_results. Each part may hold letters, digits and underscores only. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_TABLE_IN_PRODUCT_SCHEMA` | Put the results table in a schema of its own: every product writes to it, and fluid apply owns each product's schema. Create one with CREATE SCHEMA <catalog>.dq, then pass --results-table <catalog>.dq.fluid_test_results. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_TABLE_MISMATCH` | The table exists without the fluid test results columns, so nothing was written. Point --results-table at a new table name; forge creates it with the right columns. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_WRITE_FAILED` | Check DATABRICKS_HOST, the token or OAuth client, and DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID. The schema must exist and this identity needs USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA, CREATE TABLE and MODIFY on it. The test report above is unaffected: rerun fluid test once the write can succeed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_DASHBOARD_NEEDS_TABLE` | --results-dashboard draws the --results-table table: pass both. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_TABLE_NEEDS_NATIVE_ENGINE` | --results-table records the native engine's per-rule results; drop --engine soda. Or keep --engine soda and its JUnit or JSON output, without --results-table. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_TABLE_NEEDS_LIVE_CHECKS` | --results-table records the live checks of a run, and --no-data runs none. Drop --no-data to test and record, or drop --results-table. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_DASHBOARD_INVALID` | Give a workspace path whose last part is the name, e.g. --results-dashboard '/Workspace/Shared/fluid/Data quality'. The path must start with / and have no empty, . or .. parts. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_DASHBOARD_PATH_TAKEN` | Something other than a dashboard already sits at that workspace path. Choose another --results-dashboard path, or move that object away. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_TEST_RESULTS_DASHBOARD_FAILED` | The results were written; only the dashboard step failed. This identity needs CAN MANAGE on the dashboard (or write access to its folder) and CAN USE on DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_ICEBERG_CATALOG_MOVE_BLOCKED` | Run the printed `tofu state rm` commands: they release the resources from this contract's OpenTofu state and touch nothing in the cloud. Then re-run fluid apply. The released Glue database/table or Snowflake EXTERNAL VOLUME stays in place; delete it by hand only if nothing else uses it. | cli/apply.html#iceberg-catalog-move-guard |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_PLACEHOLDER_EMAIL` | Use the owning team's real address, never a guess; if there is none, delete the key (a contract needs no email: metadata.owner.email is optional). Never make an address up from a team or product name: an example.com, company.com, test@ or noreply@ address reaches nobody. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_TEMPLATE_RESIDUE` | Replace the starter value with the product's own: an id of <domain>.<name>, its owning team, its real build and its real output. Delete what the product does not need, such as the starter's builds or semantics, rather than keep the starter's. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_PLACEHOLDER_VALUE` | Replace the placeholder (TODO, FIXME, TBD, CHANGEME or <...>) with the real value, or delete the key when it is optional. When the key is required and nothing gives its value, say so (in your report, or to the owner) rather than make one up. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SDP_JOINS` | An SDP (Bronze) reads one source as it is: if the product combines sources, set metadata.productType to ADP and metadata.layer to Silver. Otherwise read the one source without the join. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SDP_CONSUMES_PRODUCTS` | An SDP (Bronze) reads source systems, never other data products: if this product builds on the product consumes[] names, set metadata.productType to ADP and metadata.layer to Silver. Otherwise delete the consumes[] entry and read the source system in the build. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_UNRENDERED_BUILD_STEP_REF` | Remove buildStepRef: it names a transformations[] step, no command runs a single step, and fluid generate schedule runs each build as one fluid apply --build-id task. To run a build after another, list that one in its builds[].dependencies. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_REQUIRED` | Add the property the message names to the object at the pointer: the schema requires it there. fluid validate <contract> --show-schema prints the schema, with the required properties of each object. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | Delete or rename the property the message names: the object at the pointer does not take it. Check its spelling and nesting against the schema: fluid validate <contract> --show-schema. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_TYPE` | Change the value at the pointer to the type the message names: a string, a number, true or false, a list or a mapping. Quote a value YAML would read as another type (yes, no, on, off, 1.0, 02:00). | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_ENUM` | Use one of the values the message lists, spelled exactly: case matters (Bronze, not bronze). | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_PATTERN` | Rewrite the value at the pointer so it matches the pattern the message shows. A value that ends in a line break fails too: a YAML \| block keeps one, \|- drops it. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_FORMAT` | Write the value in the format the message names (an email address, a date-time such as 2026-11-13T02:00:00Z, a URI), or delete the key when it is optional. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_NO_VARIANT` | The value at the pointer matches none of the shapes allowed there: compare it with the schema (fluid validate <contract> --show-schema) and fix the field that differs. For a binding, the platform decides the format and the location fields it needs. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_NOT_ALLOWED` | Delete the property the message names: this object does not take it, often because another property chose a variant without it. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_BOUNDS` | Bring the value at the pointer inside the limit the message names: a minimum or maximum, a length, a number of items, or items that must be unique. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_INVALID` | Fix the value at the pointer as the message says; fluid validate <contract> --show-schema prints the rule it broke. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_STREAMING_TYPES` | Give the nested column the type the message asks for: a struct its fields, an array its element, a map its key and value, each with a type of its own. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_MANAGED_FLINK` | Change the build or the expose the message names so the managed Flink lane can run it; the message names the field and the value it needs. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SPARK` | Change the Spark build the message names so the forge Spark runner can run it; the message names the field and what it needs. A host the operator has not listed is a warning here and a refusal when the job is compiled for apply: ask the operator to list it. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SPARK_IDENTITY` | Leave parameters.spark.executionRoleArn out to have forge create a least-privilege role for the build, or ask the operator to list the role in FLUID_SPARK_EXECUTION_ROLE_ALLOWLIST. Remove a sparkConf key that loads code, sets credentials or moves the catalog or checkpoint; ask the operator to list any other key in FLUID_SPARK_CONF_ALLOWLIST. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SOVEREIGNTY` | Move the binding into a region that sovereignty.allowedRegions lists, or widen allowedRegions when the data's residency rules allow it. A region in sovereignty.deniedRegions is refused in every enforcement mode. | concepts/sovereignty.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_AGENT_POLICY` | Change exposes[].policy.agentPolicy as the message says: the models and use cases it allows or denies must not contradict each other. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_PRODUCT_TYPE_INCONSISTENT` | Make metadata.productType and metadata.layer agree: SDP with Bronze, ADP with Silver, CDP with Gold (or set only one of them). | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_DUPLICATE_ID` | Give each output port its own contract id: change or delete the exposes[].contract.id the message names. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_COMPOSITION_VIOLATION` | Consume only products of a type this product accepts: SDP takes none, ADP takes SDP and ADP, CDP takes SDP, ADP and CDP. Or correct this product's metadata.productType if it was set wrong. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_ICEBERG_SINK` | Fix the streaming Iceberg sink field the message names; the message gives the value or the variable it needs. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SECRET_REF` | Write the secretRef in its scheme's form (the message gives it), or have the operator allow it: the message names the setting (FLUID_SECRET_SCHEMES, FLUID_SECRET_PREFIXES or FLUID_ACQUISITION_SECRET_REF_ALLOWLIST). | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_ALERTS` | Fix the alert route the message names: name the Airflow connection that holds the URL, key or password, never the value itself; give an email route its to; set alerts.sla for an sla_miss route. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_ALERT_PLUGINS` | For a plugin's kind, fix the route as the message says, or install the package that registers the kind under the fluid_build.alert_notifiers entry points. For an organisation's default routes, fix them in its pack (the fluid_build.alert_defaults entry point), let FLUID_PLUGINS_ALLOWLIST load the pack, or leave the routes out with alerts.defaults: false. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_ICEBERG_MAINTENANCE` | Fix the exposes[].iceberg.maintenance field the message names: backend spark needs a schedule and runs on the engine: spark build that writes the table (name it with build when several do); backend glue needs a roleArn and takes whole days; orphans and snapshots older than P1D. A table no forge build writes names runtime instead of build: an EMR runtime (emr-serverless, emr-ec2 or emr-eks) with its applicationId, clusterId or virtualClusterId and an executionRoleArn, and removeOrphanFiles then sets olderThan longer than its writer's longest commit delay. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_LOCATION_PATH` | Write exposes[].binding.location.path without a '.' or '..' segment: a table's location keeps it as written while a listing, a grant or a write resolves it, so x/.. reaches the parent of x. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_TABLE_POOLS` | orchestration.airflow.poolPerOutputTable gives a task one pool, so a build that writes several tables cannot be serialized with it: declare one output per build (builds[].outputs) or split the build. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_MAINTENANCE_ACTIONS` | Install the package that registers the action's kind under the fluid_build.maintenance_actions entry points, let FLUID_PLUGINS_ALLOWLIST load it, or fix the action's options as the message says. Each statement the kind returns must be one DELETE, UPDATE or MERGE whose target is the expose's own table, named fluid.<database>.<table>. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_CONFLUENT_BINDING` | Fix the Confluent (Tableflow) binding field the message names; the message gives the value it needs. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_DATABRICKS_BINDING` | Fix the Databricks binding or setting the message names (a SQL warehouse in DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID, no workspace host in the contract). | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_ICEBERG_BINDING` | Fix the Iceberg binding field the message names: a catalog kind FLUID knows, and one storage location per external volume. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_GCP_BINDING` | Fix the GCP binding field the message names; its remediation is part of the message. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_STORAGE_LAYOUT` | Fix the binding.location.partitionBy or binding.properties.cluster_by field the message names; for a note, register the table's partitions or declare the key values Athena projects. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_GOVERNANCE` | Change the governance or access-policy field the message names, or bind the expose to a platform that enforces it. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_VECTOR_BINDING` | Fix the pgvector binding field the message names (binding.vectorConfig and the columns it reads). | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_CONTINUOUS_TRIGGER` | Give a batch build a schedule trigger (type: schedule and a cron), or use an engine that runs continuously. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_BUILD_ID` | Rename the id the message names: a letter or _ first, then at most 127 letters, digits, _, - or . | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_PACKAGING` | Fix the packaging block as the message says; plan, generate iac and apply decide from the same block. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_SEMANTICS` | Write a measure's expr as the column it aggregates (agg: sum, expr: amount), never as an aggregate (SUM(amount)), which aggregates twice. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_DATA_RULES` | Fix the rule the message names: invariants, identifier formats, placeholders and shared attributes are written as RFC-data-rules.md says, their texts in FLUID SQL/1. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_EXTENSION` | Fix the extensions block the message names: the plugin that owns that key wrote the message. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR_FINDING` | The validator plugin named in brackets wrote this finding: do what it says, or ask that plugin's owner. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_OVERLAY` | Key the overlay's list entries by id (exposeId, id) instead of position, so each patch lands on the entry it means. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_CHECK_FAILED` | A check crashed, so the contract was NOT checked for what it covers: run fluid validate <contract> --verbose and report the error with the contract. | cli/validate.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_FINDING` | Do what the message says at the place it names, then run fluid validate again. | cli/validate.html |
